Author: @VPCh.
Content:
2:40 Steam from a pot is not hotter than water by any significant amount (maybe 100°C vs 99°C). Steam has a lot more energy than water, but the temperature is almost the same.
When substances change state, especially water, they release or absorb a huge amount of energy. For example, boiling or condensing water takes over 5x more energy than raising it from near-freezing to the boiling point.
So when that steam which is carrying all that energy comes in contact with the cooler vegetables, it condenses, releasing massive amounts of stored energy into the food as it changes state.
The one exception to this would be if you had it sealed so tightly that the pressure increased (hence how a pressure cooker works), but even increasing it by a single degree would require half a psi of force, which would require you to hold down that lid with about 25lbs of force.
